# core


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A vault is one SQLite file that holds everything you have collected,
such as web pages, papers, talk transcripts, PDFs, notes and source
files, all searchable together.
[`Vault()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/core.html#vault)
opens `~/.vishalakshi/vault.db`, `Vault(path)` opens or creates any
other file, and `Vault(':memory:')` makes one that lasts only as long as
the process.

A [`Vault`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/core.html#vault)
is a [litesearch](https://github.com/Karthik777/litesearch) `Index`, and
litesearch decides how text is stored and found. Each thing you add
becomes a document. A document is split along its headings into a tree
of sections, which litesearch calls nodes, and each section’s text is
cut into chunks. Every chunk is stored twice: as text, for SQLite’s
full-text keyword search, and as a vector, a list of numbers from an
embedding model that puts texts with similar meanings near each other. A
search runs both and merges the two rankings with reciprocal rank fusion
(RRF), which scores each chunk by its rank in each list rather than by
the raw scores, because a keyword score and a vector distance cannot be
compared. The default embedding model is `potion-multilingual-128M`,
which is small, fast and covers over 100 languages, Devanagari among
them; `encoder=` picks another (see [concepts](07_concepts.ipynb)).

The vault adds to that a `kind` on every document, saying how it arrived
(`web`, `pdf`, `arxiv`, `note`, `code` and so on), shelves that keep
separate collections in the same file, marks that record a person’s
judgements about a document, an entity graph and topic map, and the
methods on the other pages that fetch, read, extract and answer.

### Vault.add

``` python
def add(
    src, # text, `[(page_no, text)]`, a file path, or a directory
    title:str=None, # document title; defaults to the filename, or the first line of text
    source:str=None, # url or path; defaults to the title. Identity is hashed over it
    kind:str=None, # one of KINDS: the facet you filter and report on
    meta:dict=None, # provenance: the query that found it, when, which tier fetched it
    force:bool=False, # re-ingest a source already present
    refresh:bool=True, # re-ingest text whose content hash differs from what is filed; files refresh via `force` or `housekeep`
    **kw
)->dict: # forwarded to litesearch add_doc (chunker, summarize, with_heading)
```

*Add text, pages, a file or a directory to the vault, adding a source
again only when its content changed.*

`search` returns chunks: each hit is a short `snippet` with the
`node_id` of its section and the `doc_id` of its document. `sections`
ranks whole sections instead. `context` is what to hand a language
model: whole sections with their text, each with a breadcrumb (the path
of headings down to it, such as `Attention › Multi-head`) and a
`node_id` that `read` turns back into the full section. Its `related`
list holds sections found by vector similarity to the results rather
than by matching the question, as leads. `context` also adds a couple of
sections from each other shelf (`shelves=2`), and code sections
(`code=`) when [kosha](03_code.ipynb) has indexed the repository.
`rerank=True` reorders the hits with a cross-encoder model, which needs
the `rerank` extra (`pip install 'vishalakshi[rerank]'`).

These methods, and `read` and `document`, take `pii=`, which is `off`
unless you set it; see [pii](09_pii.ipynb). Every row also carries
`age`, the seconds since its document was filed, and `stale`, and stale
rows sort last.


*Make a retrieval method take `pii=` and `pii_ner=` and apply that

A `node_id` names a section and a `doc_id` names a document. `doc(ref)`
finds a document’s row by its id, its exact source, or part of its
title. `document(ref)` rebuilds a whole document in reading order with
its headings put back, which is what a model reads to extract fields
from; given a path the vault has never seen, it reads the file from
disk. `read(node_id)` rebuilds one section, and `toc` and `sections`
walk the tree.

A document’s `meta` holds where it came from and anything set with
`set_meta`, such as its doctype. Adding a changed document again
rewrites its meta, so a lasting judgement about a document goes in the
`doc_marks` table instead (see Marks below).

## Shelves

One vault file can hold several shelves. A shelf is a separate
collection with its own chunks, section tree and vector index, so a
large corpus on one shelf, say a thousand papers, does not crowd a small
one out of the rankings. `shelf(name)` opens a shelf, creating it the
first time. A shelf keeps the embedding model it was first written with,
and reopening it with a different one raises an error, since vectors
from two models cannot be compared. `shelves()` lists the shelves with
their models and document counts, and `drop_shelf` deletes one. The main
shelf is called `store`. `SHELVES` names the ones the vault itself uses:
`store`, `papers`, `sanskrit`, `code` and `data`. Acquisition sends some
kinds to their own shelf through `KIND_SHELF`, below.

## Marks

A mark is a judgement about one document, kept in the `doc_marks` table
so it survives the document being added again. There are three. `noisy`
is for junk such as a cookie banner or a site footer, which search,
sections, context and `ask` then leave out. `pii_override` holds the
privacy marks described on [pii](09_pii.ipynb). `stale` says a document
no longer matches its source; search still returns it, flagged and
sorted last, and the mark is lifted when the document is added again
with new content. `mark` sets any of them, and `mark_noisy`,
`mark_stale` and the pii methods are the named ways to do it. `marks()`
lists every mark on the shelf and `marks(ref)` gives the one on a
document.

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(Path(d)/'test.db', offline=True)
    assert 'vault_stores' not in v.db.t                    # litesearch's store_meta is the one registry
    test_eq(v.db._store_meta('store')['encoder'], 'hash-256')
    assert v.shelves()[0]['store'] == 'store'
```

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'test.db'
    a = Vault(p, offline=True)
    a.add('A report about polonium.', title='report')
    b = Vault(p, offline=True)
    assert b.doc('report')
    test_eq(len(b.shelves()), 1)
    assert 'feedback' in b.db.t
    assert 'rankers' in b.db.t
```

``` python
# a vault written before litesearch stamped encoders carries only `vault_stores` rows: each is copied
# into `store_meta` once, on first use, so `shelf()` still reopens with what wrote it; nothing writes them again
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'old.db'
    a = Vault(p, offline=True); a.add('A report about polonium.', title='report')
    a.shelf('papers', encoder='hash', dims=64).add('Paper about thorium.', title='paper')
    a.db.q('update store_meta set encoder=?', [''])
    a.db.t.vault_stores.create(store=str, encoder=str, dims=int, method=str, added_at=float, pk='store')
    a.db.t.vault_stores.insert_all([dict(store='store', encoder='hash', dims=256, method='hash', added_at=time.time()),
                                    dict(store='papers', encoder='hash', dims=64, method='hash', added_at=time.time())])
    b = Vault(p, offline=True)
    test_eq(b.db._store_meta('store')['encoder'], 'hash-256')
    sh = b.shelf('papers')
    test_eq((sh.enc.method, sh.enc.dims, b.db._store_meta('papers')['encoder']), ('hash', 64, 'hash-64'))
    test_eq([s['dims'] for s in b.shelves()], [256, 64])
    test_fail(lambda: Vault(p, offline=True, store='papers'), contains='Two encoders')
```

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'test.db'

    a = Vault(p, offline=True)
    a.add('A report about polonium.', title='report')
    before = list(a.marks())

    b = Vault(p, offline=True)
    assert list(b.marks()) == before
```

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(Path(d)/'test.db', offline=True)
    v.add('A report about polonium.', title='report')

    assert 'doc_marks' in v.db.t
    assert v.marks() == []

    v.mark('report', noisy=True)
    assert v.marks('report')['noisy'] == 1
    assert not v.search('polonium')
    assert v.search('polonium', include_noisy=True)
```

A shelf opened from a vault shares the vault’s embedding model in
memory, so opening many shelves loads the model once. `offline=True`, or
`$VISHALAKSHI_OFFLINE`, carries over to a new shelf as well, so an
offline vault never downloads a model.

``` python
# A shelf is a partition, not a second encoder, so it reuses the vault's live one.
from tempfile import mkdtemp

v = Vault(Path(mkdtemp())/'v.db')
s = v.shelf('project')
assert s.enc.model is v.enc.model      # the same object: a shelf per project used to cost a load each
assert s.name == 'project'

# `offline=True` has to survive into a brand-new shelf, or it does not mean "never download":
# a shelf with no registry row used to fall through to the default and load a real model
o = Vault(Path(mkdtemp())/'o.db', offline=True)
assert o.enc.method == 'hash' and o.shelf('fresh').enc.method == 'hash'

# An explicit encoder still wins, and a shelf already on disk is reopened with whatever wrote it.
r = v.shelf('papers', encoder='code')
assert r.enc.name == ENCODERS['code']
r.note('rank fusion needs only each leg ordering', title='RRF')
assert Vault(v.path).shelf('papers').enc.name == ENCODERS['code']
assert Vault(v.path).shelf('papers').search('rank fusion'), 'the reopened shelf lost its note'
print('shelf encoders:', {x['store']: x['encoder'] for x in v.shelves()})
```

`KIND_SHELF` sends documents of some kinds to their own shelf when they
are added to the main one: arXiv papers to `papers`, and Sanskrit files
to `sanskrit` when `add_dir` finds them and ganapati is installed.
`search` and `sections` look at one shelf only. `context` adds results
from the other shelves (`shelves=`), and `elsewhere(q)` searches every
other shelf directly, for when the answer may be on another shelf.

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(Path(d)/'test.db', offline=True)
    v.add('Main report about polonium.', title='main')

    papers = v.shelf('papers')
    papers.add('Paper about thorium.', title='paper')

    sql = []
    v.db.conn.set_exec_trace(
        lambda cursor, statement, bindings:
            sql.append(statement) or True
    )

    v.context('thorium', code=0, shelves=2)

    v.db.conn.set_exec_trace(None)

    ddl = [
        q for q in sql
        if q.lstrip().upper().startswith(('CREATE ', 'ALTER ', 'DROP '))
    ]
    assert ddl == [], ddl
```

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

class _Chat:
    "A scripted extraction, so the graph is the same every run and no model is asked for."
    runtime = 'litert'   # it stands in for the local default; a hosted chat builds only over an all-Open shelf
    def oneshot(self, u, **k):
        return ('{"summary":"a report","entities":[{"name":"polonium","type":"substance"}],'
                '"relations":[{"src":"polonium","rel":"appears_in","dst":"report"}]}')

with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(Path(d)/'test.db', offline=True)
    v.add("A scheduled report about polonium.", title="report")
    result = v.connect(chat=_Chat())

    assert result['entities'] > 0
    assert v.search('polonium')
    result
```

## Try it

The cells below use the default embedding model. With `offline=True` the
vault uses litesearch’s `hash_embed` instead, which needs no download
but matches spelling rather than meaning; `stats()['encoder']` says
which one is in use.

``` python
v = Vault(':memory:')
v.note('Late chunking beats naive chunking because context survives the split.', tags=['retrieval'])
v.add('# Attention\n\nScaled dot-product attention weights values by query-key similarity.\n\n'
      '## Multi-head\n\nHeads attend to different subspaces in parallel.', 'Attention', kind='note')
v.stats()
```

``` python
test_eq(v.stats()['docs'], 2)
test_eq(v.stats()['encoder'], 'model2vec')
assert v.search('chunking')[0]['snippet']
# a hit is a handle plus enough text to recognise it, not the chunk itself; the scoring
# internals the two legs disagree about (`rank`, `_dist`, `_rrf_score`, `rowid`) stay inside
_h = v.search('chunking')[0]
test_eq(sorted(_h), ['age', 'breadcrumb', 'doc_id', 'node_id', 'page', 'score', 'snippet', 'stale'])
assert len(v.search('chunking', chars=20)[0]['snippet']) <= 20
assert v.read(_h['node_id'])['text']          # the handle opens what the snippet came from
test_eq([d['kind'] for d in v.sources()], ['note', 'note'])
test_eq(len(v.sources(kind='web')), 0)
test_eq(len(v.search('chunking', kind='web')), 0)
```

``` python
d = v.doc('Attention')                          # by title substring
test_eq(v.doc(d['id'])['title'], 'Attention')   # by doc_id
test_eq(v.doc(d['source'])['title'], 'Attention')  # by source
test_eq(v.doc('nothing in here'), None)

whole = v.document('Attention')
test_eq((whole.origin, whole.nodes), ('vault', 3))   # the root, the heading, the subheading
# every section, in document order, with the headings that say what each one is
assert whole.text.index('Scaled dot-product') < whole.text.index('## Multi-head') < whole.text.index('subspaces')
test_eq(v.document('Attention', headings=False).text.find('## Multi-head'), -1)
test_eq(v.document('Attention', max_chars=20).text, whole.text[:20])
test_eq(v.document('Attention', max_chars=20).truncated, True)
# a `Pages n–m:` node title is build_tree's placeholder, not a heading the document wrote
v.add('Prose with no headings at all, long enough to chunk and to be stored in the vault.', 'plain')
assert '# Pages' not in v.document('plain').text and 'Prose with no' in v.document('plain').text

test_eq(v.set_meta(d['id'], doctype='paper')['doctype'], 'paper')
test_eq(v.doc(d['id'])['meta']['doctype'], 'paper')                 # survives the round trip
test_eq(v.set_meta(d['id'], reviewed=True)['doctype'], 'paper')     # merged, not replaced
test_fail(lambda: v.document('no such document'), contains='no document in the vault')
```

``` python
test_eq(tidy_bc('Attention › Pages 1–1: Scaled dot-product › Multi-head'), 'Attention › Multi-head')
test_eq(tidy_bc(None), '')
# a window with a blank first line leaves the placeholder bare, and it is still a placeholder
test_eq(tidy_bc('Doc › Pages 1–1: › Body'), 'Doc › Body')
```

``` python
from functools import partial
from vishalakshi.ask import CHAT_CACHE, CachedChat, use_chat
```

``` python
# the extraction replays from recordings, so the tests run without the model; VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT=1 records a miss
with use_chat(partial(CachedChat, path=CHAT_CACHE)): r = v.connect()
assert r['entities'] > 0
# `entities` is what each batch wrote and `merged` what resolution folded away again, so the rows
# left are the difference: one batch covers a corpus this size, and stats counts no topic node
test_eq(v.stats()['entities'], r['entities'] - r['merged'])
```
